newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re plans separate ART unit - paper.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re plans separate ART unit - paper.

text.p: Swiss Reinsurance Co., the world's second largest reinsurance company, plans to spin off its Alternative Risk Transfer (ART) actitivies into a separate legal unit, Swiss Sunday paper Sonntags Zeitung said.
The new unit could be named Swiss Re New Markets and will initially be 100-percent owned by Swiss Re, Sonntags Zeitung said.
The paper said Swiss Re's head of communications Otto Kern had confirmed the report.
Sonntags Zeitung speculated that Credit Suisse Group could later take a stake in Swiss Re's new company, but noted that Kern did not confirm this.

Credit Suisse Group and Swiss Re have been cooperating in the area of ART -- which combines derivative financial Instruments with insurance and risk management -- since 1995 and the two companies have formed three joint ventures in this area.
Sonntags Zeitung said Swiss Re would announce the creation of a separate ART company at the end of April.
The new company has also been evaluating the possibility of creating an exchange for the trading of derivative-based insurance products in Zurich, the paper added.
Walter Kielholz, chief executive of Swiss Re, set up Swiss Re's ART division in 1995 as part of Swiss Re's strategy to expand its activities in ART and life reinsurance.
